notes: LAUNCH-DAY read of the v4.3.2 composite (10 evaluations: AA-Briefcase v1.1, GDPval-AA v2.1, AutomationBench-AA, Terminal-Bench 4.0, SciCode, Humanity's Last Exam, GDP.pdf, CritPt, AA-Omniscience, AA-LCR v1.1). GAP-FILL (2026-09-22, same day, second pass): the initial WebFetch-summarized read only resolved claude-opus-5-5's own max/xhigh/high rows, rounded to whole numbers, with no same-snapshot comparison rows. A direct curl of the raw page HTML with a browser user-agent found the page's server-embedded Next.js RSC JSON payload (not __NEXT_DATA__ literally, but an equivalent self.__next_f.push chunked payload) containing four labeled Dataset objects at full float precision: 'Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index: Score', 'Cost per Intelligence Index Task' (USD, broken down by input/reasoning/answer/cacheWrite/cacheHit components, sum = total $/task), 'Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index: Output Tokens per Task' (broken down by reasoning/answer tokens), and 'Time per Intelligence Index Task' (timePerTask = weighted average decode minutes per task, excludes TTFT/overhead). These datasets are each a TOP-N CHART (the Score dataset lists 32 models total; the Cost/Tokens/Time datasets appear to be similarly truncated to a comparable top slice), NOT a full model roster — a model's absence from a dataset means it did not make that chart's cutoff, not that AA never tested it. Existing max/xhigh/high rows below were left as originally recorded (source_type/evidence_grade/caveat unchanged) rather than silently overwritten with the newly found higher-precision float, since both readings are the same underlying AA number at different rounding and neither supersedes the other; the raw payload values are noted in each row's caveat for anyone who needs the extra precision. claude-sonnet-5, claude-haiku-4-5, and claude-opus-5-5(low) were confirmed ABSENT from all four embedded datasets by direct string search of the JSON payload (not merely 'not visible in a fetch summary') — recorded in missing[], not fabricated as zero/interpolated scores. A secondary press citation (search-engine synthesis, not a direct fetch) reports Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra tied at 53 and Claude Opus 5 at 51 on the PRIOR v4.3 index (not v4.3.2) — different metric_id, not recorded here as a row. CONFLICT WORTH NOTING: a secondary aggregator (BenchLM.ai, mirrored via search, not fetched directly) reports a different public snapshot with GPT-5.6 Sol leading at 58.9%, Opus 5.5 second at 57.6%, GPT-5.6 Terra third at 55.0% — disagreeing with AA's own primary page on RANKING, not just score. Note the raw payload's own float for Opus 5.5 max is 57.6223698102963, i.e. BenchLM's 57.6 matches AA's own underlying float almost exactly and it is AA's own ROUNDED display (58) that diverges from AA's own raw number — the conflict is therefore AA's display rounding vs a competing model's rounding, not a BenchLM data error as such. The AA primary page is still preferred per this pack's sourcing rules; BenchLM's ranking claim is not recorded as a row, only flagged.
